H1.statement: All three operation families complete the full descriptor-to-real-runtime path.
H1.evidence: completeness_matrix.json: all 3 rows YES on descriptor/candidates/legality/cost-model/selector/fallback/policy-serialization/policy-deserialization/real-implementation-invoked, with real execution performed live this slice on all 3 targets (GPU for RMSNorm+LM-head, real vLLM server for LM-head, real Pi for MatMul).

H2.statement: All three families preserve policy serialization and fallback semantics.
H2.evidence: plan_round_trip.json: 10/10 checks pass across all 3 families in one shared plan dict; fallback candidates verified always-legal and correctly triggered for all 3 families (RMSNorm eager fallback, LM-head default GEMM, MatMul FP32 tiled).

H3.statement: RMSNorm custom CUDA execution outperforms at least one realistic non-custom baseline.
H3.evidence: rmsnorm/baseline_comparison.json: custom-selected beats torch.compile (the fastest real non-custom baseline measured; flashinfer unavailable on this GPU, vLLM's own dispatch falls through to eager) by 1.34x-2.98x at all 12/12 tested shapes.

H4.statement: RMSNorm selector-chosen block size outperforms one globally fixed block-size policy across the shape sweep.
H4.evidence: rmsnorm/baseline_comparison.json: mean ratio of best-single-global-fixed-block(512) vs selector-per-shape = 0.986, i.e. the selector is on average ~1.4% SLOWER than simply always using block_size=512 on this 12-shape sweep; selector wins clearly at only 1/12 shapes (+7.1%) and loses by up to 6.6% at others. RMSNorm's absolute cost is small and dominated by launch/memory overhead, leaving little headroom for shape-aware gains at these shapes.

H5.statement: LM-head unified selector reproduces the direct E2E-8 serving optimization.
H5.evidence: lm_head/aggregate_metrics.json: unified vs direct_e2e8 TPOT difference is -0.83% (B=1), -0.04% (B=2), -0.05% (B=4), +0.04% (B=8) -- all far inside the 3% tolerance; outputs identical across states at all 4 batches.

H6.statement: LM-head batch=1 remains within the accepted regression budget.
H6.evidence: lm_head/aggregate_metrics.json: unified vs baseline at B=1 is +0.91%, within the 3% budget.

H7.statement: MatMul selected candidates outperform FP32 fallback on at least one measured shape.
H7.evidence: matmul_bias_relu/selector_comparison.json: 2.14x-14.06x speedup vs FP32 fallback at 7/9 measured shapes (all except the 2 tiny fallback-triggering shapes, where no speedup is claimed).

H8.statement: Packed-B and Cortex-A76 specialization provide measurable benefits where selected.
H8.evidence: matmul_bias_relu/selector_comparison.json: packing alone (packed-generic vs row-major, same codegen) gives a real, consistent 1.12x-1.32x; adding cortex-a76-specific codegen on top of packing gives a further 1.94x-16.16x -- both effects are real, measured, and separated, not conflated.

H9.statement: The MatMul stability gate either achieves 9/9 production-selector agreement or remains explicitly classified as a known gap.
H9.verdict: PARTIAL, explicitly classified as a known gap (Path B chosen)
H9.evidence: matmul_bias_relu/stability_gate.json: 8/9 agreement in E2E-10's original run, 7/9 in this slice's fresh re-run (both real); the unified selector does not implement the p95/median stability gate that exists only in the original production slice3c_target_selection.select_candidate(); this is documented, not hidden, and not claimed as 9/9.

H10.statement: Selector and dispatch overhead remain negligible relative to measured optimization.
H10.verdict: SUPPORTED for RMSNorm and LM-head; PARTIAL for MatMul
H10.evidence: overhead.json: RMSNorm one-time selection ~35.5us (negligible vs any kernel call); LM-head cached dispatch 0.266us = 0.00074% of the batch=2 saving; MatMul's one-time selection cost (~3.05ms per call, plus a 1.55s one-time graph build) is LARGE relative to the smallest measured kernel latencies, and is only negligible because the architecture caches it via a static policy resolved once, not per-call (cached resolve: 0.135us, which IS negligible) -- reported honestly as a real, non-trivial cost when NOT cached.

H11.evidence: regression_tests.json: 1937 total passed across both environments, 0 unexpected failures; source hashes for all 7 generic-core files and all family-specific files unchanged from end-of-E2E-10 to start-of-E2E-11 (this slice made zero source edits, per its read-mostly mandate).

H12.statement: The repository now supports a truthful three-family optimization claim without adding a fourth family.
H12.evidence: All 3 families show a real, separately-measured optimization effect in at least one clearly-defined domain (RMSNorm: custom-kernel-vs-torch.compile; LM-head: real serving TPOT; MatMul: INT8-packed-plus-target-codegen-vs-FP32), reported separately from selector/architecture completeness per the task's explicit instruction not to conflate them. No 4th family was added (confirmed: registries hold exactly 3 entries each, per registration_audit.json).
